podcast.title: Description
podcast.body: Psychobilly is described as a crazier and more amped-up version of rockabilly music. Hassel Adkins is noted as a pioneer in this style. "If you're into psychobilly, the crazier and more amped-up version of rockabilly, Hassel Adkins was a pioneer."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Early Sound of Los Coyotes
podcast.body: Los Coyotes, one of the artists released by GASA, had an initial sound that was darker and closer to Psychobilly, before potentially evolving their style. "los coyotes, quienes sus inicios tenían un sonido más oscuro y cercano el Saiko Vili."

srcs.episode: La España Siniestra ｜ La edad de oro del Postpunk y el Dark wave

podcast.title: Genre Definition
podcast.body: Psychobilly is described as a musical genre that blends elements of punk, old-school rock and roll from the 1950s and early 1960s, rockabilly (an early form of rock and roll), and rhythm and blues. "This is a mix of punk old school rock and roll from the 50s and early 60s, rockabilly in early form of rock and roll, and rhythm and blues."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Geographical Home and Fan Pockets
podcast.body: While psychobilly has fans globally, including unexpectedly in Eastern Europe, its primary home is in the US South. "Although Psychobilly has pockets of fans everywhere, including oddly enough, Eastern Europe, its home is in the US south."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Origin and Description
podcast.body: Psychobilly is defined as a "tiny sort of bluesy garage rock" that conjures the atmosphere of a B-grade horror movie. Lux Interior and Poison Ivy of The Cramps are largely credited with the invention of this genre. "psychobilly, a tiny sort of bluesy garage rock that sounds like it belongs in a big-rate horror movie. Hell, Lux and Ivy pretty much invented psychobilly."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Psychobilly – The Cramps from NYC Punk; Real Home Now Europe (Especially Post-Soviet States); Canadian Bands: The Brains, Gutter Demons, The Creepshow
podcast.body: Psychobilly combines one part punk, one part rockabilly (country-fied early rock and roll from the 1950s), and one part schlocky sci-fi and horror movies. Tip further toward horror and you get Gothabilly; drop country elements and you get Horror Punk. The Cramps emerged from the New York punk stew of the 1970s as the kings of psychobilly, but psychobilly's real home has become Europe — first the UK, then eastern Europe (East Germany, Poland, Bulgaria, and former Soviet satellite states). Canadian contributions include The Brains, the Gutter Demons, and The Creepshow, the last of which mines horror movie themes. "Most of these flavors also have themes of sex and violence in common, and more than a few ditch electric-based guitarists for upright double bases."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Punk Substyle
podcast.body: Psychobilly is identified as one of several sub-styles that emerged as the punk movement spread globally after its mid-1970s inception. "el Psycho Billy."

srcs.episode: Egg Punk: Explorando el lado más raro del punk

podcast.title: Punk with Rockabilly and Horror
podcast.body: Psychobilly is a form of punk music characterized by an "old-time rockability feel" that is grittier than traditional rockabilly. A key element of its aesthetic is a "fascination with horror movies." "Psychobilly was a form of punk that had an old-time rockability feel, but was even more gritty. Plus, it had a fascination with horror movies."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The Post-Punk Explosion Part 7: All the rest

podcast.title: Term Coined by The Cramps
podcast.body: The Cramps coined the term "Psychobilly" to promote their concerts on posters and flyers, and it rapidly evolved into a recognized musical genre. This term encapsulated their unique blend of rockabilly, protopunk, and a dark, campy aesthetic. "El término Psycho Bill Lilloy con Yoron para promocionar sus conciertos en carteles y flyers y rápidamente se convirtió en un género musical."

srcs.episode: Amor, Terror y Psychobilly: La Historia de The Cramps

podcast.title: The Cramps' Distinction from Other Psychobilly Bands
podcast.body: When The Cramps toured the UK, they encountered other bands categorizing themselves as psychobilly. However, The Cramps emphasized that their only common ground with these bands was shared conceptual references, and they did not share the fast and violent sound that characterized many of these other groups. "Cuando viajaron al reino unido de gira, para su sorpresa, había varias bandas que se englobaban dentro del género, pero ellos defendían que lo único que tenían en común con esas bandas eran las referencias, no compartían su sonido rápido y violento."

srcs.episode: Amor, Terror y Psychobilly: La Historia de The Cramps
